sn22.86:4.2: “Here, venerable sir, I stay in a wilderness hut not far from the Buddha.
sn22.86:4.3: Then, venerable sir, several wanderers of other religions came up to me … and said this to me:
sn22.86:4.4: ‘Reverend Anurādha, when a Realized One is describing a realized one—a supreme person, highest of people, who has reached the highest point—they describe them in these four ways—
sn22.86:4.5: After death, a realized one still exists, or no longer exists …
sn22.86:4.6: or both still exists and no longer exists, or neither still exists nor no longer exists’”
sn22.86:5.1: Having said this, venerable sir, I said this to those wanderers:
sn22.86:5.2: “Reverends, when a Realized One is describing a realized one—a supreme person, highest of people, who has reached the highest point—they describe them other than these four ways:
sn22.86:5.3: ‘After death, a realized one still exists’ …
sn22.86:5.4: ‘neither still exists nor no longer exists’
sn22.86:5.5: When they had said this, venerable sir, those wanderers of other religions said this to me:
sn22.86:5.6: ‘That mendicant must be junior, recently gone forth, or else a foolish, incompetent senior mendicant’
sn22.86:5.7: Then, after rebuking me by calling me “junior” and “foolish”, those wanderers of other religions rose from their seats and left.
sn22.86:6.1: Soon after those wanderers of other religions had left, venerable sir, this occurred to me:
sn22.86:6.2: ‘If those wanderers were to inquire further,
sn22.86:6.3: how should I answer them so as to repeat what the Buddha has said, and not misrepresent him with an untruth? How should I explain in line with his teaching, so that there would be no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism’”
